evidence.detail: Repository HEAD exactly matches the launcher-bound target commit.
The target record exists and identifies roadmap v6 as DRAFT pending Codex review and human approval.
Reviewed the approved brief, roadmap, all proposed M4 work items, current-state record, workflow/security governance, and the existing analyzer and normalization contracts.
evidence.reference: project/brief/PROJECT_BRIEF.md; ROADMAP.md; project/issues/ISSUE-0015.md; project/issues/ISSUE-0016.md; project/issues/ISSUE-0017.md; project/issues/ISSUE-0018.md; project/status/CURRENT.md; rules.py; graph.py

evidence: ROADMAP.md:231 marks M3 COMPLETE under DECISION-032.
ROADMAP.md:234-241 immediately states that M3 is not COMPLETE, its milestone reviews have not run, and ISSUE-0014 may still be pending.
This contradiction prevents the roadmap from being a reliable current-state and dependency record for M4, whose dependency is M3 COMPLETE.
findings.remediation: Remove or rewrite the obsolete M3 paragraph so it consistently records M3 as complete and accepted under DECISION-032.
findings.title: Roadmap contradicts itself about the M3 prerequisite
findings.verification: Re-read the milestone and M3 sequence sections and confirm every M3 status, gate, and next-action statement agrees with DECISION-032.

evidence: ROADMAP.md:232 defines M4 and binds ISSUE-0015 through ISSUE-0018 to it as planned work.
Each proposed issue still says `Milestone: None yet` and claims no roadmap version currently covers the work.

The workflow requires issue records to identify their roadmap and milestone before implementation; retaining these assertions after v6 approval would leave the durable work-item records contradictory.
findings.remediation: Set each issue's milestone to M4 and describe roadmap v6 as the pending, not-yet-approved governing roadmap candidate. Keep implementation explicitly blocked until exact human approval and separate issue-start authorization.
findings.title: M4 work-item metadata denies the roadmap association that v6 establishes
findings.verification: Confirm ISSUE-0015 through ISSUE-0018 consistently name M4 and roadmap v6 while retaining PLANNED status and both human gates.

evidence: ISSUE-0016 defines PASS whenever a scoped policy has a non-empty `grantControls.termsOfUse`.
The proposed rule does not require `grantControls.operator == "AND"`; with an OR grant-control operator, Terms of Use may be an alternative rather than required.
The proposed tests cover only absent versus non-empty Terms of Use and therefore cannot detect this false pass.
The scope definition also does not state how excluded users or roles affect whether a policy is meaningfully scoped.
findings.remediation: Define effective scope including relevant exclusions and require semantics that actually make Terms of Use mandatory, including appropriate handling of the grant-control operator. Add negative tests for an OR-combined Terms of Use control and for excluded target scope.
findings.title: Terms-of-Use rule can pass when acceptance is optional
findings.verification: Run analyzer tests showing that a scoped AND policy requiring Terms of Use passes, while an OR policy where Terms of Use is only an alternative and a policy excluding the claimed target scope do not pass.

evidence: ISSUE-0017 says to union enabled admin-scoped policies and then require `each covering policy` to satisfy the session controls, which is ambiguous when compliant and non-compliant policies overlap.
ISSUE-0018 uses the same formulation for authentication strength.

The existing `_check_mfa_for_admins` first filters qualifying policies and unions their included roles, but it ignores `excludeRoles` and all-users policies; copying it verbatim does not establish effective coverage of every admin role.
The planned tests cover full included-role union but do not cover exclusions, all-users coverage, or overlapping compliant/non-compliant policies.
findings.remediation: Specify a single effective-coverage algorithm for both rules: determine which policies satisfy the required control, compute the admin roles each such policy effectively covers after inclusions and exclusions, and require their union to cover the governed admin-role set. Explicitly decide how `includeUsers: ["All"]` and exclusions contribute. Add tests for exclusions and overlapping qualifying/non-qualifying policies.
findings.title: Admin-rule coverage semantics are ambiguous and can misstate effective role protection
findings.verification: Run tests proving excluded roles are not counted, overlapping weak policies do not invalidate coverage supplied by qualifying policies, uncovered roles fail, and the documented treatment of all-users policies is enforced.

evidence: M4 changes the analyzer response contents and README-facing rule count at the project milestone level.
ROADMAP.md:232 requires only Python tests, Python compilation, and governance validation for the frozen M4 candidate.
The repository's established frontend checks exercise consumption of `/api/analysis`, and AGENTS.md lists `cd frontend && npm test` plus the UI build as project commands.
A milestone general review must cover integration and regressions, but the M4 exit criteria omit executable frontend/build regression evidence.
findings.remediation: Add `cd frontend && npm test` and a reproducible frontend build check (`npm ci` or the repository-approved clean-install equivalent followed by `npm run build`) to the M4 frozen-candidate exit criteria, or explicitly justify and obtain human agreement for excluding them.
findings.title: M4 milestone verification omits the frontend integration checks
findings.verification: Record successful frontend test and build results against the same frozen M4 candidate used for the Python and governance checks.

limitations: No external Microsoft documentation was accessed because network access is restricted. ISSUE-0018 appropriately requires fresh implementation-time verification of the authentication-strength ID, so that external fact remains unverified in this review.
Implementation checks were not run because this is a roadmap review of unimplemented work; feasibility was assessed against the committed source and current test contracts.
Review scope focused on the proposed v6/M4 delta while checking completed milestones and governance records for dependency consistency.
review.summary: Target identity is valid, and M4 is broadly feasible and appropriately decomposed, but the roadmap is not ready for approval. It contains contradictory milestone/work-item state, underspecifies rule semantics in ways that can produce false posture results, and omits frontend integration checks from the M4 frozen-candidate gate.
